findings.claim: The smoke check 'hermes not rerouted' cannot show that a Hermes chat makes no classifier call, though the plan's outcome, ADR 0029 and the component page all claim it. The tier rules are router-only, so a Hermes chat keeps its model even if the classifier runs for it (spike 2's exact failure mode). Bifrost reports the classifier call in extra_fields.routing_metadata.calls as a request_type 'decisions' entry (spike 1 stdout). The Hermes check should assert no such entry, and the router check should assert one is present, with a stub test for each.

test_router_key's cloud-suffix scan covers only the classifier, the routing-rule targets and the router key. Row r3 covers every model name in the jobspec and every virtual key in services.tf. It skips the hermes, memex and openviking keys' allowed_models and the provider keys' models lists, so adding 'gpt-oss:120b-cloud' to the Hermes key would pass. Today they are all '*', so the row holds, but the test would not catch a regression there.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan says.
The config.json router block matches the spike 4 config that worked (same keyword shape, same rule order and CEL, with the suffix-free names from spike 7).
The timeout "3s" parses under upstream ComplexityDecisionConfig.UnmarshalJSON at transports/v2.3.1.
jev-latest is in the static typesafe catalog.
The Jev secret already exists in Vault, so the new template block will not hold the alloc.
There are two non-blocking gaps: the live smoke cannot prove the "no classifier call" claim (f1), and the r3 suffix scan is narrower than the row (f2).
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: pre_commit pass, cli_tests pass, rows r1-r4 pass, "stamp green: e40a0c02f7b8...e42".

`scripts/tf_validate.sh`: deployments/applications "Success! The configuration is valid." The router key's allowed_models are alphabetical and its provider_configs are in order, so a second plan should be clean.
Missing-secret risk: consul-template's `with secret` on a missing KV v2 path errors and blocks the render.
Bifrost has a static port and a pinned host, so applying before the secret existed would take the gateway down.
I checked `vault kv metadata get secret/default/bifrost/typesafe`: version 1 was created 2026-11-15 by userpass-operator, and the field set is exactly ['TYPESAFE_API_KEY'].
The path is under the job's own default/bifrost/ prefix, like the other provider keys.
The risk does not apply here.
Re-registering the job: the jobspec edit is intended.
It restarts Bifrost once, and `null_resource.bifrost_ready` re-polls /health through its jobspec hash before any virtual key is touched.
That is the existing pattern.
Upstream source at transports/v2.3.1 (scratchpad checkout): the decision timeout accepts a duration string, and the typesafe catalog lists jev-latest.
Spike shapes: the smoke's decision body matches spike 7's ollama_live.sh, and the routing_info.model values match spike 4's output (bare model name, no provider prefix).
The Hermes check expects "deepseek-v4.1-flash", which is right.
Rows: r1, r2 and r3 tests parse the real heredoc and Terraform and assert each fails_when clause, except the r3 gap in f2.
The stub-HTTP tests cover both branches of the router and Hermes smoke checks.
r5 (judgment): the config can meet the decisions, tier-routing and plan-clean parts, and the smoke covers decisions, the two tier prompts and the Hermes model.
It cannot show "no clef call" for Hermes (f1).
r6 (judgment): ADR 0029 exists with the alternative it rejected.
The component page and the smoke docstring match the config.
f1: the Hermes smoke check passes even when the classifier runs for Hermes.
Assert no 'decisions' entry in extra_fields.routing_metadata.calls for the Hermes chat, and assert one is present for the router chats.
f2: widen the r3 cloud-suffix scan to every virtual key block in services.tf and every provider key's `models` in the jobspec.
ADR 0029 says a new tier model must also go on the router key's list "or the key refuses it".
No spike tested a routed target outside the key's list, because every spike key listed all the tier models.
The advice is harmless, but the claim is untested.
